Let \(p=2027\) and \(m=\frac{p-1}{2}=1013\). Define

\[
a_k=\binom{2k}{k}2^k.
\]

We want

\[
S=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} k a_k \pmod p.
\]

First note that for \(k>m\), we have \(p\le 2k<2p\) while \(k<p\), so \(p\mid \binom{2k}{k}\). Hence those terms vanish modulo \(p\).

For \(0\le k\le m\), use \(m\equiv -\frac12\pmod p\):

\[
\binom{m}{k}
=\frac{m(m-1)\cdots(m-k+1)}{k!}
\equiv \frac{(-1/2)(-3/2)\cdots(-(2k-1)/2)}{k!}.
\]

Thus

\[
\binom{m}{k}
\equiv (-1)^k \frac{1\cdot 3\cdots (2k-1)}{2^k k!}
=(-1)^k \frac{(2k)!}{2^{2k}(k!)^2}
=(-1)^k 4^{-k}\binom{2k}{k}.
\]

So

\[
\binom{2k}{k}2^k\equiv (-8)^k\binom{m}{k}\pmod p.
\]

Therefore the polynomial

\[
F(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} a_k x^k
\]

satisfies

\[
F(x)\equiv \sum_{k=0}^{m}\binom{m}{k}(-8x)^k=(1-8x)^m \pmod p.
\]

Since \(S=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} k a_k = F'(1)\pmod p\), we get

\[
S\equiv \frac{d}{dx}(1-8x)^m\bigg|_{x=1}
=-8m(1-8)^{m-1}\pmod p.
\]

Now \(2m=p-1\equiv -1\pmod p\), so

\[
-8m=-4(2m)\equiv 4\pmod p.
\]

Also \(1-8=-7\) and \(m-1=1012\) is even, hence

\[
S\equiv 4\cdot 7^{1012}\pmod{2027}.
\]

To evaluate \(7^{1012}\), use the Legendre symbol. Since

\[
2027\equiv 3\pmod 4,\qquad 2027\equiv 4\pmod 7,
\]

quadratic reciprocity gives

\[
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)
=-\left(\frac{2027}{7}\right)
=-\left(\frac{4}{7}\right)
=-1.
\]

Thus

\[
7^{1013}\equiv -1\pmod{2027},
\]

so

\[
7^{1012}\equiv -7^{-1}\pmod{2027}.
\]

Since

\[
7\cdot 1448=10136=5\cdot 2027+1,
\]

we have \(7^{-1}\equiv 1448\pmod{2027}\). Therefore

\[
7^{1012}\equiv -1448\equiv 579\pmod{2027}.
\]

Finally,

\[
S\equiv 4\cdot 579=2316\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
